markdown.markdown:
This five-lesson course builds the computational model of working memory used in the
N-Back fMRI study from the ground up. Each lesson adds one layer — from the memory buffer
to the decision model to parameter fitting to brain regressors — ending with a complete
understanding of every line in `scripts/nback_model.py`, `03_fit_model.py`, and
`04_regressors.py`.

### Lessons

| Lesson | Title | Key concepts |
|--------|-------|-------------|
| 1 | Working Memory as a Decaying Buffer | Activation function; δ and μ; buffer depth; δ as encoding probability |
| 2 | From Activations to Decisions | SDT; probit model; β and σ; trial-type predictions; α identifiability |
| 3 | Interference, Normalisation, and Attentional Control | Lure evidence; δ–σ confound; interference normalisation; probit-normal correction |
| 4 | Fitting the Model | Negative log-likelihood; parameter transforms; Nelder-Mead; AIC/BIC; M3 selection |
| 5 | From Parameters to Brain | Maintenance; control demand; lure activation; encoding surprise; prediction error; FSL format |

### Prerequisites

- Intermediate Python (NumPy, SciPy, Pandas)
- Basic familiarity with the n-back task and fMRI GLMs
- No prior computational modelling experience required

### Dependencies

```bash
pip install numpy scipy pandas plotly
```
